title: Verb patterns: -ing or to?
tagline: Some verbs need -ing, some need to, and a few change meaning depending on which one you pick.
why: The verb right after enjoy, want, decide or hope has to be in the correct form, and B1 Preliminary uses exactly this choice as a distractor in the multiple-choice cloze. It also matters every time you write an email about your plans or talk about your hobbies in the Speaking test — get enjoy to play or want going wrong and it sounds instantly foreign.

hook.text: Liam: "I enjoy playing football, but I hate running." Sofia: "Really? I want to try the new dance class. Do you fancy coming?" Liam: "Maybe — but I promise to think about it!"
hook.ask: Look at the verbs in bold. Some are followed by an -ing form (playing, running) and some by to + verb (to try, to think). Can you guess which first verb — enjoy or want — decides the pattern?

diagrams.title: Which pattern does the verb take?

rows.label: stop
cells: pause in order to do something else

rows.label: try
cells: make an effort to do something difficult

diagrams.title: How to choose the right pattern

steps.label: Add the second verb in the right form
Watch remember/forget/stop/try — the meaning changes
steps.ex: I stopped to buy milk ≠ I stopped buying milk

head: Pattern
Verbs
Example
rows: enjoy, finish, avoid, mind, suggest, keep, practise
want, decide, hope, promise, learn, agree, plan
I stopped to answer the phone. / I stopped answering messages.
My parents let me stay up late.
good at, interested in, keen on, afraid of, instead of

examples.text: Mateo enjoys playing the guitar every evening.
I can't avoid seeing him — we're in the same class.
Nadia hopes to travel to Cusco this year.
We decided to walk instead of taking the bus.
Liam promised to help with the project.

use.point: Same verb, different meaning: remember, forget, stop, try

examples.text: I stopped eating meat two years ago.
On the way home, I stopped to buy some bread.
examples.note: paused in order to do something else

examples.text: Please remember to bring your project tomorrow.
I remember meeting Miss Vega on my first day.
My parents let me stay at Sofia's house.
examples.note: let + person + base verb, no to
make + person + base verb, no to

examples.text: Nadia is really interested in learning French.

watch_out.why: enjoy is always followed by -ing, never to + verb.

watch_out.wrong: She wants going to the party.
watch_out.right: She wants to go to the party.
watch_out.why: want is always followed by to + verb.

watch_out.wrong: I stopped to smoke five years ago (I don't smoke any more).
watch_out.why: stop + -ing = end a habit; stop + to = pause to do something else.

watch_out.wrong: My mum let me to go out.
watch_out.why: let and make take the base verb, with no to.

watch_out.wrong: Liam is good at play chess.
watch_out.why: After a preposition (at, in, on…), verbs always take -ing.

watch_out.wrong: I finished to do my homework.
watch_out.why: finish is always followed by -ing, like enjoy.

l1.why: Spanish uses the infinitive after disfruto, but enjoy always takes -ing in English.

l1.wrong: I hope going to the party.
l1.right: I hope to go to the party.
l1.why: hope needs to + verb, not -ing, even though it feels similar to other -ing verbs.

l1.wrong: My parents let me to go out.
l1.why: Spanish dejar + infinitive sometimes adds a, but English let never uses to.

l1.wrong: I finished to do my homework.
l1.why: Spanish terminar de + infinitive becomes finish + -ing in English, not finish to do.

remember.trick: Enjoy, finish, mind → -ING. Want, hope, decide → TO!
remember.tip: Learn the two lists like a short song. If a verb isn't on either list, the safer guess is usually to + verb.

dialogue.title: The summer job advert
dialogue.context: Liam has found an advert for weekend jobs at a new café and tries to convince Sofia and Nadia to apply with him.

lines.speaker: Liam
lines.text: Look at this advert! They want to hire three students for the weekends.

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.text: I don't know… I hate waking up early on Saturdays.

lines.speaker: Liam
lines.text: But you enjoy talking to people, and you're really good at it!

lines.speaker: Nadia
lines.text: I'd love to try it, actually. I need to earn some money for my trip.

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.text: OK, I promise to think about it tonight.

lines.speaker: Liam
lines.text: Great! Don't forget to bring your ID when we apply.

lines.speaker: Nadia
lines.text: And we should avoid arriving late — that never makes a good impression.

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.text: Fine, I've decided to apply. Let's go together tomorrow.

lines.speaker: Liam
lines.text: Perfect! My parents will let me stay out a bit later for it.

lines.speaker: Nadia
lines.text: Mine too, as long as I keep doing well at school.

can_do: I can use -ing after verbs like enjoy, finish, avoid and mind.
I can use to + verb after verbs like want, decide, hope and promise.
I can use remember, forget, stop and try correctly, choosing -ing or to for the right meaning.
summary: Some verbs are always followed by -ing: enjoy, finish, avoid, mind, suggest, keep, practise.
Some verbs are always followed by to + verb: want, decide, hope, promise, learn, agree, plan.
Remember, forget, stop and try change their meaning depending on -ing or to.
make and let take the base verb with no to; verbs after a preposition always take -ing.
